reference_answer: NASA defines systems engineering as a methodical, multidisciplinary approach for the design, realization, technical management, operation, and retirement of a system.

A system is a combination of elements that function together to produce a capability needed to meet a need. Elements can include hardware, software, equipment, facilities, personnel, processes, and procedures.
System-level value is created largely by the relationships and interactions among elements, so optimizing one subsystem in isolation can harm overall system performance.
They are system design processes, product realization processes, and technical management processes.
